citations.review_text:
Beautiful game and wonderful experience. I guess it really resembles the wild because it is really easy to get lost and difficult to navigate around. Also if you're an achievement collector like me; the achievements are bugged and you'll only get them when playing in one session. You cannot exit out of the game and it's recommended to turn off autosave. You can get all optional achievements in free roam mode (after completing the game once) except for Love Turts. 
7.5/10

It is a great game and definitely worth the €5 I spent. The scenery is beautiful, the set pieces make sense, and the music is fitting. The story is quite interesting, although it can be a bit annoying at times. Some plot points drag on for a bit too long. All in all, a good game to spend time on. Too bad the Ol' Shoshone achievement is borked or glitched. It does not pop when grabbing and listening to the tape. 

There are very minor technical issues, such as micro stutters (but only when entering a different area, so it is forgiven) and very occasionally a floating tree. For the most part, however, the scenery is very well put together and the terrain has no major flaws. There is no ability to jump without a climb/drop prompt, but that is probably for the better (mainly avoiding softlocks behind rocks, in ravines or in bushes).

beautiful game with awe inspiring atmosphere and sound design
initially I was bored because of all the constant walking from A to B across the map, but the game grew on me really fast with the story. for such a short game, it was very enjoyable.
the game doesn't have amazing support for tiling window managers, and I had to tinker with my settings a ton to get fullscreen to work properly without rendering issues
once I completed the story, I found myself having to restart my game multiple times to get the achievements in free roam, because apparently alt tabbing disables achievements for the session

the game is very peaceful and and very short as well which is something i look for when i barely finish most story games i touch due to my horrible attention span, i enjoyed this for what it is, what i didnt enjoy was the bugged movement and achievements, seriously what kind of game has bugged achievements? other than that I had fun and enjoyed the virtual nature

I played this game back in 2024 and loved the story and the relationship developed by the main characters.
And now I came back to it in 2026 to 100% it and I felt as if I had fallen in love with this game just like the first time I played it.

I say that everyone should play this game and experience its story at least once in their life time.
Thank you Dev team for this awesome experience!

My first play through took be around 2.4 hours, but getting the remaining achievements took almost double the time. The story is entertaining and worth the 5 or so hours I played.

Most require you to save and repeat the event to activate it. For example the camera one where you have to take 18 shots, but most you can get in the free roam mode with no problem.

citations.review_text: Story is short but intriguing. Ran into a couple of bugs that made things difficult. Refresh rate has to be locked at 60hz otherwise you may get stuck, but otherwise a fine game.
really good game, ran into some bugs with clipping into the ground and getting stuck but should be fixed with v-sync

Awesome short experience. 8/10.


Originally I watched a youtuber's playthrough in 2019, then I played about halfway through the game on console back in 2022. So then, I thought, what better time to beat the game than in summer? What an emotional experience it was. The game is really calm and relaxing, but can get surprisingly creepy at times. Also, it has great voice acting. For all those reasons, I consider this game to be classic to me.

However, there is a movement bug where you can't walk unless you enable V-Sync and change your Refresh Rate to 120-144hz to fix it apparently. That's what I saw online, and it's what worked for me.

This game is wonderful! Great story, relaxing but very interesting story with nice atmosphere and really cool graphics. According to my preferences, its a 10 out of 10.

But one thing ruins it all. The movement is extremely bugged, apparently it has to do with v-sync, other players has had success in putting it on or off/on, but no matter what i do i cant get it to work. Since this game is old there has been plenty of time for the devs to fix it. This game is unplayable for me and i wish i didnt have to uninstall it. It started showing later in the game and i cant proceed anymore. Its like an invisible object is in the way, sometimes it can be worked around it by strafing left or right in the desired direction but now its impossible to get by it. Thats the only reason for a negative review and im sorry i have to uninstall this potentially wonderful game.

Edit, fixing the fps/movement issue in adrenaline made this game playable again, although i think the developers should fix this issue. Im changing my review to positive!

claims.claim: The gameplay relies heavily on walking and navigating the terrain using a physical map and a compass without on-screen minimaps or location markers.

citations.review_text: Really compelling, while I'm a little late to the party in terms of discussing this game. I think it still holds up extremely well due to the visual aesthetic of the game. Additionally, the gameplay is still quite unique and is something I would love to see done again. I love hiking, so naturally I greatly enjoyed the game being purely about navigation of the world they create for you. However, regardless of my personal interest in nature, this aspect still puts quite a heavy load on both the atmosphere and story to keep you engaged, and I think they both do that spectacularly. The writing for the main characters, I would say, takes a second to really get going, but I think once you're there, it does become this comfort to speak with Delilah, especially as the game goes along. I really enjoyed my time with this game despite its brevity, as it wraps up well and leaves you wanting more. Can't wait to see what the studio does next!

Fantastic game with an interesting story and lovely artstyle. Loved using the map to navigate the world and listening to the voice acting. I quite like how this game (kinda spoiler) deprives the player of certain things happening and knowing a few things.

mixed feelings about this game. 

+++++plus+++++

- beautiful scenery to immerse yourself in. hiking with a map and taking pictures closely resemble real life experience

- good music and lighting to build up the atmosphere that goes well with the story beats

- easy achievements. one play through will get most of them unlocked. the other ones are easy to obtain with an extra 30 min of free roam mode

- once you finish, there are lots of theories around the story to dig into

- interesting around-game features. you can email yourself the camera roll and even order prints. there's also an audio tour mode with dev commentary. pretty cool stuff!

-----minus-----

- early on it could be frustrating to navigate. the views are not that distinct or memorable so it's easy to get lost without constantly checking the map. also invisible walls!

- motion sickness every time the hopping / rope tossing animations came up. i wish there's a way to disable those animations. 

- delilah. she was unprofessional, nosy, and too flirtatious. i was just there to do the job. she knew i was not available but kept harassing me even when i tried to shut her down whenever i could.
[spoiler]she was either very incompetent or completely lying to me to protect herself and ned:
- not aware of wapiti station when it was in her tower's LOS
- did not listen to me and made poor decisions that could've gotten us in trouble
- thought replacing the radio could stop someone from tuning into that frequency[/spoiler] 
just a total disaster of a coworker that i could not trust 

- there's certain things in the game where i felt like wasn't even fleshed out, like the devs forgot about it? game gave me a fishing pole and yet i could not fish. missions also get hard interrupted half way and then next day you wake up with a different mission.

[h2]Nota Geral | Overall Rating[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]Firewatch é a prova de que uma narrativa bem escrita, apoiada por uma dublagem excepcional, consegue carregar uma experiência inteira sem precisar de combate, puzzles complexos ou qualquer artifício de jogabilidade tradicional. A Campo Santo criou algo raro: um jogo sobre duas pessoas conversando por rádio em meio a uma floresta isolada de Wyoming, e mesmo assim consegue construir tensão, mistério e um vínculo emocional genuíno entre Henry e Delilah que fica na cabeça muito depois dos créditos subirem. É uma das melhores experiências narrativas que já joguei.[/b]

[i]Firewatch is proof that a well-written narrative, backed by exceptional voice acting, can carry an entire experience without needing combat, complex puzzles, or any traditional gameplay tricks. Campo Santo created something rare: a game about two people talking over radio in the middle of an isolated Wyoming forest, and it still manages to build tension, mystery, and a genuine emotional bond between Henry and Delilah that stays with you long after the credits roll. It's one of the best narrative experiences I've ever played.[/i]

[h2]Jogabilidade | Gameplay[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]A jogabilidade é minimalista de propósito, focada em exploração e no simples ato de caminhar pela floresta usando mapa e bússola pra se orientar. O que faz isso funcionar tão bem é como o rádio se torna a verdadeira mecânica central: cada decisão de diálogo com Delilah muda sutilmente a dinâmica entre os dois personagens, e a simplicidade da jogabilidade nunca atrapalha, ela só existe pra servir a história, que é onde o jogo realmente brilha.[/b]

[i]The gameplay is deliberately minimalist, focused on exploration and the simple act of walking through the forest using a map and compass to find your way. They were right when they say that affordable indie experiences change you. I got this game for the whopping sum of 3.90 bucks and every minute of those 3 hours 20 where met. I knew the game from somewhere — at this point I don't even bother trying to remember how I heard about stuff. The game just doesn't let me down. It was a short while and that's why I wanted to play it since I just 100% completed Gran Turismo 4 a week ago. It just gives me so much immersion for what it is that it just deserves a spot up there, the only other game that had me on a paper map with a compass was Far cry 2 which is an outliar in terms of ubisoft. The graphics were also gorgeous and really did get the most of what a Wyoming sunset looks like. As for the music it's a really strong point here, everytime a song cam on breaking the quietness of the wild it just sent chills down my spine and that's because one it's amazingly fitting for this american pastoral scene but secondly also because as far as the detective work and the plot go, this just had me on my damn toes — the prime example would be the first time you get to see that shadow meddling around at your tower. And here the real shiner let's be real is the story, talking about which I found the gameplay really fitting unlike some people who were really annoyed at the thought of a "walking simulator" as they call it" and yeah that's what you get for your picturesque setpiece, but if I really wanted to play something high octane I would rather be on Metal gear rising or something man. So yeah, the laid back slower paced roaming around really helped me take in those aforementioned visuals and sound (nice tortoise by the way). It starts with a kind of RPG choice based intro to set you up in the world putting in the process the weight of a dementia affected wife and not so young dog that I did get to pick. Although you never get to see said wife (you do see a picture in the tower) more on that in a bit, you get to se…

I really enjoyed playing this short, atmospheric game.

The story is bittersweet, the world is beautiful, and the game does a great job of building tension and suspense at key moments. The characters are complex and endearing, and the voice acting is absolutely phenomenal.

The main gameplay loop is essentially a walking simulator. You complete one objective at a time by hiking from point A to point B, then back again, repeating the process throughout the game.

My only real complaint is the navigation. The map isn't huge, but it's almost entirely made up of dense forest, and the game doesn't hold your hand at all. There's no minimap, so you're forced to rely on a physical map and compass that your character has to pull out every single time you want to check your location. While this certainly adds to the realism and immersion, players with a poor sense of direction (like me) will probably spend a lot of time lost and wandering around. I could have finished the game in about four hours if I hadn't spent so much time trying to find my way and backtracking.

Overall, it was a very enjoyable experience. I recommend it to anyone looking for a relaxing, atmospheric game with beautiful scenery, plenty of hiking, a touch of mystery, and excellent dialogue between its characters.

Firewatch is a breathtaking, deeply immersive adventure that hooks you immediately with its stunning wilderness setting and masterful voice acting. The emotional dialogue makes every conversation feel profoundly real. However, if you are looking for a game where your choices actually shape a satisfying, grand conclusion to all the buildup, the anti-climactic finale may leave you wishing for more agency.

I went into Firewatch not really knowing what to expect, and it ended up being one of those games that sticks with you. The conversations between Henry and Delilah felt so real that I actually found myself looking forward to every radio call. It never felt forced or overly dramatic.

The world is gorgeous too. Walking through the forest while the story slowly unfolds is surprisingly relaxing, even when things start getting creepy. The atmosphere does a great job of making you feel isolated without relying on cheap scares.

I know some people weren't happy with the ending, neither was i. Why couldn't she just wait a minute? I actually wanted to see how she looks like after speaking to her over the radio for so long!!

If you're looking for fast-paced gameplay, this probably isn't for you. But if you enjoy games with great writing, memorable characters, and a story that stays with you after you finish it, I'd definitely recommend giving Firewatch a try.

A engaging and compelling narrative driven game, let down by poor pacing and threadbare exploration.

The core of Firewatch is an engaging character study excellently performed by Rich Sommer (Henry)
and Cissy Jones (Delilah). Their performance is the driving force of the narrative and really helps sell the developing relationship of the two leads. The two only communicate via radio and thus it is up to the player to control how much Henry reports to the disembodied Delilah. It's a testament to the strength of the performance that I looked forward to every snippet of conversation and every piece of witty banter.

Unfortunately their performance is let down by gameplay that, in many ways, is substandard. Firewatch belongs to genre that is (often dismissively) referred to as 'walking simulators'. While I personally have no problem with a game taking a more narrative focus, moving away from more challenge and skill based engagement, the strength of such games is often determined by the interweaving of environment and narrative. In this regard I found Firewatch lacklustre. The national park that Henry finds himself is surprisingly lifeless, often serving as little more than padding between narrative encounters. While there are some lite navigational challenges, Firewatch rarely rewards exploration. Straying from the beaten path often only serves to pad playtime.

Despite this, Firewatch remains a pretty comfortable recommend. The strength of the core performances are so strong, and the game short enough, that the lack of engaging gameplay or exploration should not be enough to deter anyone looking for a narratively rich experience.  

(Plus you get to name a turtle 'Turt Reynolds' which is worth half a star on its own)
